one_month_reasoning: The window ends 2026-11-08, a Sunday, so the effective date is the Nov 6 close. (1) Q3 2026 results. No date has been announced: Paycom's IR page lists no upcoming event as of Oct 11 (src 36), and there is no 8-K after Aug 5 (src 12). Last year Q3 results came out Nov 5, 2025 (src 4), so a report by the Nov 6 close is likely (~85%, judgment) but not certain. I removed the Nov 4 date from round 1 because it came from a key-gated feed. The last print moved the stock +23.55% in a day (Aug 6, 2026; src 16), and the bar is now higher: consensus FY26/FY27 EPS is $12.10/$13.97 and the average target of $220 sits below spot (src 14). PEAD after August's surprise argues for slight upward drift, but the effect has weakened (src 34). I dropped my round-1 list of 12 earnings-day moves because it was computed from a key-gated feed the gate cannot reopen. (2) FOMC on Oct 27-28, after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (src 35). A further hike helps float income (~$105M FY26 guide, src 1) but raises discount rates: roughly neutral. Polymarket odds (src 26) are context only. (3) October jobs report on Nov 6 (src 31); September unemployment was 4.2% (src 30). Model: 85% earnings-in-window component (80% core, sigma 11.5% and drift +0.8%; 20% guide-shock tail, sigma 24% and drift -2%) plus 15% no-earnings (sigma 11%). Mixture mean is +0.3% and sd ~14.4% (vs 13.1% from 46%/3.5), giving P(>=spot) 0.515 and a fatter left tail.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E (17.0x Oct-2027 NTM non-GAAP EPS of $15.02 = $255) plus 40% DCF (normalized, SBC-adjusted unlevered FCF of $531M in 2026 growing 8/7/6/5/4.5%, 3% terminal, 9.0% WACC, horizon net debt $245M, 45.07M shares = $236.5). Blend $248.

methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct 2027 $15.02 (FY27 consensus $13.97, FY28E $15.37) x 17.0x (HCM/payroll/PEO peer median 17.09x, range 12.64-22.09x)

inputs_detail.derivation: S&P Global consensus on StockAnalysis, +15.45% on FY26 $12.10. Re-opened Oct 11. I dropped the key-gated Alpha Vantage cross-check.

13.97 x 1.10. FY27 consensus revenue growth is +7.44% (src 14), plus margin gain from the FY26 ~46% adj. EBITDA margin guide (src 1). The share count is already down to 45.07M (src 8), and there is $1,655.5M of buyback capacity left (src 10), which adds a little. 10% is well below FY27's +15.45%, which includes the full-year effect of the H1-2026 share shrink.

The 8-name HCM/payroll/PEO peer median is 17.09x (12.64-22.09x). PAYC is at 17.68x today (src 13), and its own forward P/E was 16.17x at FY2025 (src 15). 17.0x is at the median, so no premium is paid: PAYC's above-peer EPS growth mostly reflects the one-off 2026 share shrink, and its revenue growth (7.4%) is peer-like. The highest-in-set margin offsets the extra leverage ($900M revolver) and founder concentration, so neither a premium nor a discount. methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: 2026 normalized unlevered FCF $594M less SBC $63M = $531M; growth 8/7/6/5/4.5% to 2031; 3% terminal; WACC 9.0%; value at Oct 2027; horizon net debt $245M; 45.07M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Aggregator TTM figure (OCF less capex) through Q2 2026. [citation gate 2026-10-12: relabelled from 'reported' to 'estimate' (Paycom does not report a TTM FCF; the aggregator page shows $575.1M). Filings arithmetic: TTM OCF 678.9 - 305.0 + 427.6 = $801.5M less TTM capex 270.9 - 99.4 + 54.9 = $226.4M = $575.1M (FY25 8-K Ex.99.1, source 3; 10-Q R7, source 9). Paycom's own definition also deducts intangible purchases (FY25 $4.5M).]

inputs_detail.input: TTM OCF excluding one-off tax inflow
inputs_detail.derivation: TTM OCF = 575.1 + 226.4 = 801.5. Less the H1-26 'income taxes, net' +$74.8M (src 9, vs +$5.6M in H1-25) = $726.7M. Slightly conservative, since the 2025 overpayment behind that refund depressed H2-25 OCF.
H1-26 capex/revenue = 54.9/1,103.1 = 5.0% (src 9, 8). Add 1pt for H2 seasonality and data-centre spend, then apply to the FY26 revenue guide midpoint of $2,204.5M (src 1): $132.3M.
726.7 - 132.3 = 594.4. TTM after-tax interest is small (borrowing started in 2026) and is not added back, which is conservative.

inputs_detail.input: SBC deducted as an economic cost

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus revenue growth is +7.44% (src 14), plus ~0.5pt margin gain in 2027, fading toward terminal.
Long-run nominal growth, well below the 5.22% 10-year yield (src 32).

Ke = 5.22% (src 32) + 0.89 x 4.20% (Oct 1, 2026 ERP, src 33) = 8.96%; 0.89 is the Blume-adjusted 0.83 5Y beta (src 13). Kd = (4.00% upper fed funds after the Sep 16 hike, src 29/35, + 1.625% mid revolver margin, src 6) x 0.75 = 4.22%. Debt weight = 900 / (900 + 232.22 x 45.07M) = 7.9%. CAPM WACC = 8.58%. I add ~0.4pp (judgment) for seat-compression/AI-disruption risk, evidenced by the market pricing INTU at 12.64x and ADBE at 9.02x forward P/E (src 23, 25). I cut this from round 1's +0.86pp because the IGV drawdown behind it came from a key-gated feed. Sensitivity: 8.58% gives $254.6; 9.5% gives $218.0. [citation gate 2026-10-12: INTU 12.64x and ADBE 9.02x are StockAnalysis aggregator forward P/Es (the pages show them); INTU is 12.34x on the rebuilt NTM basis. They support a judgment only.]
Long-term debt $900.0M - cash $198.0M (10-Q, Jun 30, 2026). Operating leases ($82.8M) are excluded because lease cost is already in OCF.

Next-12-month cash FCF 594.4 x 1.06 = $630M, less after-tax revolver interest of $38M (900 x 5.625% x 0.75) = $592M. Less SBC-dilution offset of $68M (holding the share count flat) and dividends of $68M (45.07M x $1.50, src 7) = $457M retained. 702 - 457 = $245M. Buybacks instead of paydown would be value-neutral at fair value.
10-Q cover: 45,071,619 at Jul 28, 2026, incl. 786,338 restricted shares. Held flat; retained FCF is credited to net debt, not to the share count, to avoid double-counting.

Cash flows for the years starting Oct 2027 are 0.25/0.75 blends of fiscal years: 604, 642, 675, 706, 735. Discounted mid-year at 9.0% = $2,707M. Terminal = 735 x 1.03 / 0.06 = $12,611M, PV $8,196M. EV = $10,904M; less $245M net debt = $10,659M / 45.07M = $236.5.

bear.story: The seat-software de-rating returns: the market already prices INTU and ADBE at 12.6x and 9.0x forward. Hiring stays weak (Sep unemployment 4.2%), and the Feb 2027 FY27 guide comes in soft at ~5-6% revenue growth, so NTM EPS slips to ~$14.0 at 12x = ~$168. That is just above the pre-Q2-print closes ($164-175). $1.66B of no-expiry buyback capacity (10-Q) cushions it, but adding to a $900M revolver draw limits how hard Paycom can lean in.

base.story: Revenue grows ~7-7.5% (consensus) and the margin holds near the ~46% FY26 guide. Buybacks continue modestly from the $1.66B authorization, giving NTM EPS of ~$15.0 by Oct 2027 at ~16.6-17x (the 17.09x HCM peer median): ~$250, about +8% from $232. This matches my $248 fair value; most of the 2026 re-rating is already in the price.

bull.story: Automation and AI features lift retention and attach, so revenue growth goes back to ~9-10%. The Sep hike and any further ones lift float income, and Paycom uses more of the $1.66B authorization. NTM EPS of ~$15.5 at ~20.5x (between ADP's 22.1x, the top of the peer range, and the median) = ~$318.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium or discount. Paycom has the highest margin in the set (~46% FY26 adj. EBITDA guide). Against that, its revenue growth (7.4% FY27 consensus) is peer-like, its above-peer EPS growth is mostly the one-off, debt-funded 2026 share shrink (10.9M shares bought for $1.42B in H1, 10-Q), and it now carries a $900M revolver. A median multiple fits that balance. Only 8 peers: once non-HCM names (ADBE, BL, TYL) are dropped, which round 1 used as AI-disruption analogues, few genuine listed US HCM/payroll comparables remain. The rest are micro-caps (e.g. ASUR) or non-US platforms with different growth profiles. ADBE's 9.0x is kept only as evidence for the WACC risk add, not in the median.

thesis_break_reason: $155 is 11.1x FY27 consensus EPS of $13.97, below every HCM/payroll/PEO peer (lowest is INTU at 12.64x). It is under the $163.96 Jul 31 close, so it erases the whole Q2 re-rating and more, and it sits back in the Feb-Jul 2026 range when the stock traded near its $104.90 low. A close there would most likely mean the EPS path broke: a FY27 guide (Feb 2027) at or below ~5% revenue growth, retention falling, or employment contracting. Ordinary 46%-vol noise is less likely to explain it. I moved it up from $150 because the confirmed $1.66B no-expiry buyback capacity makes a fall that deep without bad news less likely. Leverage is not the trigger: net debt is ~$702M.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor found a factual error in my round 1: the buyback authorization did not expire. I confirmed at source that a new $2.0B plan was approved May 4, 2026 with no expiry (8-K) and that $1,655.5M was available at Jun 30 (10-Q R33). I rewrote the bear and bull stories and raised the thesis break from $150 to $155. I also verified 45.07M shares (10-Q cover, incl. restricted stock), $702M net debt excluding leases (10-Q balance sheet), and the +$74.8M one-off tax inflow, $31.6M SBC and $54.9M capex in H1 OCF (10-Q R7). On top of that I built my own normalized FCF from the 10-Q rather than the call-recap '$650M' figure. Comps: I accept that ADBE, BL and TYL are not HCM peers. The 8-name HCM/payroll/PEO set (with BBSI checked at source) has a 17.09x median, so my 17x is at the median, not a margin premium. Fair value falls from $260 to $248: P/E $255 (unchanged EPS path) and DCF $268 to $236.5 (normalized and SBC-adjusted FCF, 45.07M shares, $702M rolled to $245M net debt, 9.0% WACC after a smaller disruption add). The scenario mean is $246.5 (168/250/318 at 25/50/25). Base rates: I removed every number computed from key-gated Twelve Data pulls (12-month return base rates, IGV drawdown, earnings-day history). The distribution now anchors on facts the brief and public pages give: 46% realized vol, a 52-week range of $104.90-244.98, the brief's ±25-35% typical large-cap 12-month move, the verified +23.55% Aug 6 earnings move, and a sell-side average target ($220) below spot, which usually lags after sharp re-ratings. Ladder: 50% a lognormal with median $238 and sigma 0.40, plus 50% a scenario mixture (each scenario lognormal, sigma 0.17-0.20), with a fat-tail floor at the lowest strikes. P(>=232) is 0.557, about unchanged from 0.556. The lower fair value pulls it down; removing the wrongly bearish buyback-expiry story pushes it up. I disagree mildly with the supervisor's 16.75x (2% below median): no evidence in the verified record supports that specific discount, so I stay at the median. Prediction-market odds (Polymarket) are context only and enter no number. Lane share: 22 of 36 sources are in-lane.
